title: cairn-fires-its-clock-probes-on-its-own-pulse
intention: The cairn device fires its own clock probes (history_integrity, trouble_panel_surfaces_live_troubles) from its groundloop/pulse.py on each heartbeat, so they run again now that the heartbeat no longer discovers probes/.
why: Since bae622881f03 PROVED (2026-09-30) the heartbeat no longer discovers probes/ folders; it calls only groundloop/pulse.py files. So history_integrity, trouble_panel_surfaces_live_troubles are dark: the only firing left is one pass at web-server start through bus_client's private GroundLoopDevice, which ticket efb670ff1dd8 removes. That is the lived symptom: history_integrity compares every component's working-copy history.json/state.json against HEAD between crossings (the at-rest half of the build_inspector sieve); trouble_panel_surfaces_live_troubles checks that the cairn device's trouble pane can reach the trouble lane over the bus and come back with live troubles, and nobody is looking.
traces_to: Law 6 and Law 1 via ticket bae622881f03 (PROVED 2026-09-30): the heartbeat calls each groundloop/pulse.py and nothing else, and Akien ruled clock probes are 'tickled by the system device or their owning devices (from the ground loop pulse)'. The owner fires its own watch.
how: FIRST build the shared tool cairn/tools/base/beat_probes.py: BeatProbes(device_id, folder, names, bus) loads exactly the named modules' PROBE from <folder>/probes/ (re-loading one when its mtime changes), and on_pulse(now, context) fires them through a minimal concrete BaseShim (cairn/tools/base/shim.py) so crossing memory, while_true, cleared-on-enough, and loud refusal are the shim's existing semantics and are not re-derived. The heartbeat keeps pulse modules loaded between beats (heartbeat.Triggers), so a module-level BeatProbes holds that memory. The bus is injected: a pulse.py passes cairn.tools.bus_client.connect_bus(devices=[], beat=False), created once per process. Then write cairn/devices/cairn/groundloop/pulse.py: a module-level BeatProbes('cairn', <this folder>, ['history_integrity', 'trouble_panel_surfaces_live_troubles'], bus) and on_pulse(now, context) returning its pulse record. Only the named probes fire; nothing else in the folder is touched. The probe files stay where they are, unchanged.
falsifier: Proof cairn/devices/cairn/proofs/test_groundloop_pulse.py plus cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_beat_probes.py: (helper) a stub probe whose trigger stays true pokes once across two beats, a while_true one pokes each beat, a raising trigger is recorded and the rest still fire, a probe whose enough holds is cleared, and a name with no module is recorded as missing, never raised; (1) discovery.pulse_sites() lists cairn/devices/cairn/groundloop/pulse.py at class level; (2) the module's BeatProbes names exactly ['history_integrity', 'trouble_panel_surfaces_live_troubles'] and each resolves to a Probe; (3) other modules in cairn/devices/cairn/probes/ are not in its roster; (4) on_pulse(now, {}) with a recording stub bus returns a record whose fired+held entries cover exactly those probes. Live horizon: three consecutive beats of ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/machines/ground_loop/liveness.json list the cairn trigger ok. Wrong intent if one of these probes turns out to be event-driven rather than clock-driven.
watchme: none, because the probes being moved ARE the watches (cairn/devices/cairn/probes/history_integrity.py, cairn/devices/cairn/probes/trouble_panel_surfaces_live_troubles.py), each keeping its own ticket's WATCHME, and whether they fire is read on every beat in the heartbeat's own record ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/machines/ground_loop/liveness.json (the cairn trigger's ok flag and pulse record).
assumption_check: (1) history_integrity, trouble_panel_surfaces_live_troubles are clock probes (Akien's group-2 list, 2026-09-30). (2) The heartbeat calls on_pulse(now, {}) once per 60s beat and holds the module between beats, re-loading it when cairn/devices/cairn/groundloop/pulse.py changes, which resets crossing memory; a reset re-pokes a still-true condition once, which is acceptable and matches a loop restart under the old runner. (3) A probe's poke needs a bus; connect_bus(devices=[], beat=False) gives one without beating. (4) The probe files are unchanged; only who fires them moves.
missing_check: (a) The helper must record a named probe with no module as missing rather than raise, so a renamed probe is loud on the heartbeat's record. (b) What the pulse returns lands in liveness.json through json.dumps(default=str); the shim's pulse record is plain dicts, so this holds. (c) The nine other owner tickets depend on this one; they are cast now and wait for it at BUILDME.
builder_check: WHERE: new cairn/tools/base/beat_probes.py and its proof cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_beat_probes.py; new cairn/devices/cairn/groundloop/pulse.py and cairn/devices/cairn/proofs/test_groundloop_pulse.py. SHAPE of a pulse.py: see cairn/machines/counting_block/groundloop/pulse.py (on_pulse(now, context) -> dict). FIRING: subclass BaseShim minimally (device_id property, probes() returning the loaded list, and whatever abstract members BaseShim declares: read the class before writing), then call its on_pulse; do not copy its body. LOADING: import each <folder>/probes/<name>.py by path with a synthetic module name, read module.PROBE. BUS: from cairn.tools.bus_client import connect_bus; bus = connect_bus(devices=[], beat=False), once per process, lazily on the first beat. TESTS use a stub bus with a post() that records. DO NOT touch the heartbeat, the probe files, or other devices' folders.
